newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Foreign funding banned for Indonesian parties.
newsitem.headline: Foreign funding banned for Indonesian parties.

text.p: Indonesia has banned political parties contesting the May 29 general elections from obtaining foreign aid, the Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Wednesday.

"It is against the law for the parties to ask for foreign funds even though they feel that the (government) election funding is insufficient," the newspaper quoted H.S.A. Yusacc, a spokesman for the Interior Ministry, as saying on Tuesday.
Ministry officials were not available for comment on Wednesday.
The two minority parties complained on Monday that the 500 million rupiah ($208,333) given them by the government for the forthcoming general election was not enough.
Ismail Hasan Metareum, head of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP), said the government funding, which makes up most of the minority parties' income, was too small.

Surjadi, leader of the government-backed faction of the divided Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), said the 500 million rupiah would not pay for the four-week campaign, which begins officially on April 27 and ends on May 23.
Yusacc was quoted by Media Indonesia as saying the government could freeze the activities of political parties that received foreign funding. It gave no more details.
The minority parties have long complained that the ruling Golkar, whose leaders are drawn from senior government figures and leading business people, has no problems funding its extensive activities.
Even before the official campaign period, Central Java province is awash in yellow Golkar flags with members of the party hosting pop music concerts.
The two minority parties, the PPP and the PDI, usually rely on donations from supporters to fund their daily activities.
